key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants such as Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and modifying lattice structure.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical materials-design lever for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells, helping balance conductivity, CO2/SO2 resistance, and thermal stability.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic-radius effects
Assessment of proton uptake, vacancy formation, impurity-phase formation, and gas adsorption
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence that Ca doping lowers A–O bonding strength, increases oxygen-vacancy formation and proton uptake, and reduces adsorption of acidic gases while improving stability-related metrics.
watch_item: The benefits may depend on the degree of Ca segregation and on whether proton transfer is the rate-limiting step in the target electrolyte architecture.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
